statement: About a given circle to circumscribe a square.
heath_proof: Let ABCD be the given circle; thus it is required to circumscribe a square about the circle ABCD. Let two diameters AC, BD of the circle ABCD be drawn at right angles to one another, and through the points A, B, C, D let FG, GH, HK, KF be drawn touching the circle ABCD. [III. 16] Then, since FG touches the circle ABCD, and EA has been joined from the centre E to the point of contact at A, therefore the angles at A are right. [III. 18]  For the same reason the angles at the points B, C, D are also right. Now, since the angle AEB is right, and the angle EBG is also right, therefore GH is parailel to AC. [I. 28]  For the same reason AC is also parallel to FK, so that GH is also parallel to FK. [I. 30]  Similarly we can prove that each of the straight lines GF, HK is parallel to BED. Therefore GK, GC, AK, FB, BK are parallelograms; therefore GF is equal to HK, and GH to FK. [I. 34] And, since AC is equal to BD, and AC is also equal to each of the straight lines GH, FK, while BD is equal to each of the straight lines GF, HK, [I. 34]therefore the quadrilateral FGHK is equilateral. I say next that it is also right-angled. For, since GBEA is a parallelogram, and the angle AEB is right, therefore the angle AGB is also right. [I. 34] Similarly we can prove that the angles at H, K, F are also right. Therefore FGHK is right-angled. But it was also proved equilateral; therefore it is a square; and it has been circumscribed about the circle ABCD. Therefore about the given circle a square has been circumscribed.
ai_proof_text:
4.7
**Statement:** About a given circle to circumscribe a square.

**Step 1.** Let ABCD be the given circle. Take E, the centre of the circle ABCD (3.1).

**Step 2.** Take any point A on the circumference, join AE (P1), and produce AE to meet the circumference again at C (P2). From the point E on AC draw EB at right angles to AC (1.11), so that the adjacent angles AEB, BEC are right (D1.10), and produce BE to meet the circumference again at D (P2). Since AC and BD are drawn through the centre E and are terminated in both directions by the circumference, they are diameters of the circle (D1.17). The angle CED is vertical to the angle AEB, and the angle DEA is vertical to the angle BEC; hence the angles CED, DEA are also right (1.15). Thus the two diameters AC, BD are at right angles to one another, and all four angles AEB, BEC, CED, DEA at E are right.

**Step 3.** Through A draw a straight line at right angles to the diameter AC at its extremity A (1.11), and produce it in both directions (P2); call it FG. In the same way draw GH through B at right angles to the diameter BD, HK through C at right angles to the diameter AC, and KF through D at right angles to the diameter BD, each produced in both directions (1.11, P2). A straight line drawn at right angles to a diameter of a circle from its extremity touches the circle (3.16, Porism); therefore each of FG, GH, HK, KF touches the circle ABCD, at A, B, C, D respectively. Let the adjacent tangents meet one another at G (FG with GH), H (GH with HK), K (HK with KF) and F (KF with FG).

**Step 4.** By construction the angles at the points of contact, namely GAE, GBE, HCE, KDE (and the angles adjacent to them), are right. The straight line EA falls on the two straight lines FG, BD and makes the interior angles on the same side, GAE and AEB, together equal to two right angles; therefore FG is parallel to BD (1.28). The straight line EB falls on GH, AC and makes the interior angles GBE, BEA together equal to two right angles; therefore GH is parallel to AC (1.28). Likewise EC falls on HK, BD with the interior angles HCE, CEB together equal to two right angles, so HK is parallel to BD (1.28); and ED falls on KF, AC with the interior angles KDE, DEC together equal to two right angles, so FK is parallel to AC (1.28).

**Step 5.** Since each of FG, HK is parallel to the same straight line BD, FG is parallel to HK (1.30); and since each of GH, FK is parallel to the same straight line AC, GH is parallel to FK (1.30).

**Step 6.** Consequently the quadrilaterals GACH, ACKF, FGBD, BHKD have their opposite sides parallel (Steps 4 and 5) and are parallelograms; and so likewise are GBEA, HBEC, KCED, FDEA, each having its sides lying along one of the tangents and one of the diameters.

**Step 7.** In the parallelogram GACH the opposite sides GH, AC are equal (1.34); in the parallelogram ACKF, FK is equal to AC (1.34); in the parallelogram FGBD, GF is equal to BD (1.34); and in the parallelogram BHKD, HK is equal to BD (1.34).

**Step 8.** Since E is the centre of the circle, the straight lines EA, EB, EC, ED drawn from it to the circumference are equal to one another (D1.15). AC is made up of AE, EC and BD of BE, ED; adding equals to equals, AC is equal to BD (CN2).

**Step 9.** Therefore GH and FK, each equal to AC, and GF and HK, each equal to BD, are all equal to one another (CN1). Hence the quadrilateral FGHK is equilateral.

**Step 10.** In the parallelogram GBEA the opposite angles AGB and AEB are equal (1.34), and the angle AEB is right (Step 2); therefore the angle at G is right. Similarly in the parallelogram HBEC the angle BHC is equal to the angle BEC, in KCED the angle CKD is equal to the angle CED, and in FDEA the angle DFA is equal to the angle DEA (1.34); and each of the angles BEC, CED, DEA is right (Step 2). Therefore the angles at F, G, H, K are all right, and the quadrilateral FGHK is right-angled.

**Step 11.** Being both equilateral and right-angled, FGHK is a square (D1.22). And each of its sides FG, GH, HK, KF touches the circle ABCD (Step 3); therefore the square FGHK has been circumscribed about the given circle ABCD (D4.4). Q.E.F.

Path note: the tangents are constructed as perpendiculars at the extremities of the diameters (1.11 together with the Porism to 3.16), so the right angles at the points of contact follow directly from the construction rather than from the tangent-radius theorem; the sides of FGHK are compared with the diameters through the four parallelograms GACH, ACKF, FGBD, BHKD, which requires 1.30 to pass from the four basic parallels to the parallelism of opposite tangents.
